original_value: Diabetes is one of today’s greatest global problems, and it is only becoming bigger. Constant measuring of blood glucose level is a prerequisite for monitoring glucose blood level and establishing diabetes treatment procedures. The usual way of glucose level measuring is by an invasive procedure that requires finger pricking with the lancet and might become painful and obeying, especially if this becomes a daily routine. In this study, we analyze noninvasive glucose measurement approaches and present several classification dimensions according to different criteria: size, invasiveness, analyzed media, sensing properties, applied method, activation type, response delay, measurement duration, and access to results. We set the focus on using machine learning and neural network methods and correlation with heart rate variability and electrocardiogram, as a new research and development trend.

result.paraphrase: Diabetes is among the world’s most serious health challenges, and its impact continues to grow. Continuous monitoring of blood glucose is essential for tracking glucose levels and determining diabetes treatment plans. The standard method of measuring glucose is invasive, requiring finger pricking with a lancet, and it can be painful and annoying, particularly when done every day. In this study, we review noninvasive glucose-measurement approaches and offer several classification categories based on different criteria: size, invasiveness, analyzed media, sensing properties, applied method, activation type, response delay, measurement duration, and access to results. We emphasize machine learning and neural network methods, along with correlations to heart rate variability and electrocardiogram, as an emerging research and development trend.
